Project case studies

Behind every design is a problem to solve. Here is the thinking behind selected projects: the challenge, the creative solution, the final design and the services involved. These are self-initiated concept projects, not paid client commissions.

Logo and brand identity · concept project

Verdant Café

The design challenge

A new café needed to feel fresh and welcoming, yet premium enough to stand out from casual competitors. The mark had to work on a shop sign, a paper cup and a staff apron.

The creative solution

A steaming cup paired with two leaves links the name to freshness and warmth. Deep green and champagne gold lift the brand above the everyday, and a refined serif wordmark with the line “Good food. Great vibes.” keeps it friendly. Using only three colours keeps it consistent across every material.

Halo Fashion House

The design challenge

A fashion label needed a mark that feels exclusive, yet stays recognisable when shrunk onto a clothing tag or stitched onto a shirt.

The creative solution

A bold H monogram crossed by a gold arc, the “halo”, gives a simple shape that survives at small sizes. Black and gold signal luxury, while widely spaced lettering adds calm confidence. The mark was applied to a hang tag, shopping bag and apparel to prove it works in use.

Crestview Estates

The design challenge

A real estate firm must signal trust and permanence from the first glance, and combine the idea of “home” with reaching a higher view.

The creative solution

A house sits inside a monogram C, so the home is literally held by the brand. Dark green communicates stability, gold suggests value, and a strong serif wordmark keeps it dignified. A set of simple icons explains each service, and the system carries onto signage and business cards.

Brand identity and packaging · concept project

Lumen Bakery

The design challenge

A bakery needed warmth and craft without looking rustic or generic. The identity had to carry across a bag, cup, box and counter cards.

The creative solution

A single wheat leaf above a clean serif wordmark gives a calm, natural feel. Warm browns and cream echo baked goods, kraft paper reinforces the handmade story, and a soft wave pattern on the box adds movement. The line “Freshly baked. Always better.” closes every piece.

Business materials · concept project

Zenith Logistics

The design challenge

A logistics company must communicate speed and reliability, and look consistent across letterhead, folders, business cards and staff ID.

The creative solution

A bold Z built from two angled planes suggests direction and forward motion. Navy builds trust while teal adds energy. A diagonal stripe repeats on the letterhead and cards, so every item feels like part of one organised system.

Services involved

Logo designLetterheadBusiness cardsPresentation folderStaff ID badge

Product and packaging design · concept project

Pure Spring Water

The design challenge

A bottled water brand has to look clean and trustworthy in a crowded market, and still read clearly on transparent plastic.

The creative solution

A mountain and wave mark signals source and purity. Royal blue with a thin gold edge adds quality, and a large wordmark with a clear size panel makes the product easy to recognise at a glance. The system was tested on the bottle, a 12-pack and an advert.

Client policies and timelines

Clear terms from the start, so every project runs smoothly.

  • 70% deposit before work begins.
  • Two minor revisions are included. Extra revisions are charged.
  • Urgent delivery adds 30–50% to the price.
  • Printing and delivery are charged separately.
  • Final files are delivered after full payment.
  • Logo: 3–5 days
  • Flyer, poster or social post: 1–2 days
  • Brand identity: 7–10 days
  • Packaging or company profile: 7–14 days
  • Monthly packages: weekly delivery schedule
